title: Hamra' al-Asad & Moral Recovery
subtitle: Pursuit, Psychological Fortitude, and Divine Renewal after Uhud
summary: What Chapter 40 did not linger on: Bukhari 4077 on the seventy who followed the enemy after Uhud, the classical account of Ma'bad al-Khuza'i, the verse that says 'the people' rather than 'the hypocrites,' and the separate report about not being stung twice.

sections.text: Chapter 40 has already told the morning pursuit to Hamra' al-Asad, the halt of about three days, and the fires lit so the camp would be seen. This chapter does not repeat that outline, and it does not restore a count of the fires. Sahih al-Bukhari 4077, from Aishah, is narrower than the sirah. After Uhud the Prophet feared the Quraysh might return. He asked who would go after them. Seventy men volunteered, among them Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr. The report is linked there to the verse, 'Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after injury had struck them' (3:172). It does not name Hamra' al-Asad, and it does not contain the saying about being stung twice.

The classical biography adds the condition that only those who had fought the day before were to go out, and it names wounded men, including Talhah, among those who answered. The withdrawal of a large group with Abdullah ibn Ubayy at Uhud is also part of that biographical account. Bukhari 4077 gives the number who went out as seventy. It does not give a number for those who had stayed behind.

Ibn Hisham places the halt at Hamra' al-Asad, a short march south of Madinah, and says fires were lit so the camp would be seen. No checked Hadith fixes how many fires there were. The point of the sirah is the impression of a camp that had not collapsed, not a tally of the flames.

The same biographical account says Abu Sufyan had halted at al-Rawha and that some of the Quraysh spoke of turning back. Ma'bad ibn Abi Ma'bad al-Khuza'i, not yet Muslim, is reported to have seen the Muslim camp and then gone on to the Quraysh. Khuza'ah had old ties with Banu Hashim. What follows is the sirah's account of that meeting, not a wording from Bukhari 4077.

In that account Abu Sufyan asked Ma'bad what was behind him. Ma'bad told him that Muhammad had come out with a gathering Ma'bad had not seen the like of, and that the Quraysh would see the horses before they could move on. Abu Sufyan is reported to have given up the idea of returning to Madinah and to have taken the coastal road toward Makkah.

The sirah adds that he sent riders of Abd al-Qays with a threat that the Quraysh were gathering against the Muslims. The camp at Hamra' al-Asad did not scatter. The Quran then says that this increased them in faith. The verse uses the word 'the people.' It does not itself say 'the hypocrites.' Tafsir discusses who those people were. That discussion is not the wording of the verse.

الَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ فَاخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَانًا وَقَالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
'Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it increased them in faith, and they said, "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."' (Surah Al Imran 3:173)

The classical sirah reports that Abu 'Azza al-Jumahi was taken again at this time. He had been captured at Badr, released, and had then gone out at Uhud. The biography says he asked to be released once more and was not. A different Hadith, Bukhari 6133, in the Book of Manners, records from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said, 'A believer is not stung twice from one and the same hole.' That report does not mention Abu 'Azza or Hamra' al-Asad. The sirah is what joins the saying to this encounter. Bukhari 4077 does not.

The Muslims then returned to Madinah. The pursuit had shown that the defeat at Uhud had not left the city open. The details beyond the seventy who went out remain the classical biography, and they stay marked as such.

references.title: The Holy Quran
references.author: Surah Aal-Imran (3:172–175)
references.notes: Divine praise for those who responded to Allah and His Messenger after suffering wounds.

references.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
references.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH)
references.source: Kitab al-Maghazi, Hadith 4077; and Kitab al-Adab, Hadith 6133
references.notes: 4077 is Aishah's report that seventy men, including Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr, followed the enemy after Uhud. It does not contain the saying about being stung twice. That saying is Bukhari 6133, a general report from Abu Hurayrah, not a narration of Abu 'Azza.

references.title: Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah
references.author: Ibn Hisham (d. 218 AH)
references.source: Vol. 2: Ghazwat Hamra' al-Asad wa Khabar Ma'bad al-Khuza'i
references.notes: Classical account of Ma'bad, the fires without a fixed number, the riders of Abd al-Qays, and Abu 'Azza. These details are not in Bukhari 4077.
